title: bug: a trailing-newline database password silently initializes a different PostgreSQL credential
description:
Found during parent task-7693a195c01e45088b8545478aebd51f step6 live probe (full reproducible source in its comments): postgres:17-alpine starts healthy with a trailing-newline POSTGRES_PASSWORD but TCP psql using the exact supplied bytes fails authentication, before and after controlled-3. Normal and space/$/trailing-space controls authenticate, wrong-password controls refuse; all disposable resources removed.
Choose explicit fail-closed validation or supported exact-byte delivery at the owning input/init boundary; do not repair inline in the metadata-secrecy leaf. No value-bearing evidence may be persisted.
definitionOfDone: Reproduce against the actual generated scaffold and pin the precise unsupported-input or authentication boundary without logging planted values.

Reject unsupported newline-bearing database passwords explicitly before successful initialization, or demonstrate exact-byte authentication for them; retain normal/special-character positive controls, wrong-password rejection, and complete teardown.

implementationPlan.description:
REFUSE BEFORE INITIALISATION, AT THE ONLY SEAM THAT SEES THE TRUE BYTES (controlled-profile-root-templates.ts).

Add a guard service to the generated `docker-compose.yml` that reads the mounted secret and refuses when it contains a newline, and make the db service wait for it:
- The guard mounts the SAME secret (`source: POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `target: postgres_password`). The mounted file carries EXACT bytes — the sibling measured byte equality — so this is the one place the true value is visible before the entrypoint mangles it.
- The check counts newlines and prints none of the value: `wc -l < /run/secrets/postgres_password` is 0 for a value with no newline anywhere. Refuse with a nonzero exit and a message that names POSTGRES_PASSWORD and says a newline is not supported, and says WHY in one clause — the database initialises the value without its trailing newline, so the credential the operator holds is not the credential the database has.
- Reuse `postgres:17-alpine`, already pulled for the db service, so the guard costs no extra image.
- Gate the db on it with `depends_on: { <guard>: { condition: service_completed_successfully } }`.

SCOPE IT TO THIS SECRET, NOT TO ENVIRONMENT VALUES IN GENERAL. Step 1 measured why: the candidate delivery path round-trips newlines correctly and multi-line values are legitimate there. This guard is about one value whose consumer cannot round-trip it.

NEVER PRINT THE VALUE (epic rail 3, and both DoD clauses). `wc -l` reports a count; do not `cat`, do not echo the file, do not interpolate it into the message. Say the same thing in the compose comment so the next editor does not reach for `echo`.

DO NOT RESURRECT THE `x-` FIELD. `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?...}` in an `x-` key refuses correctly on unset but LEAKS the supplied value into `docker compose config` — measured on the sibling row (its comment-3e35496a) and rejected there.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE UNSET GUARD. The sibling's measured refusal must survive verbatim: `docker compose up --detach db` with unset AND empty exits 1 with stderr exactly `secret "POSTGRES_PASSWORD" must declare either ` + "`file`" + ` or ` + "`environment`" + `: invalid compose project`. Adding a service the db depends on must not change it; step 4 re-measures it.

WHY `grep -qx 0` AND NOT `test "$(wc -l ...)" -eq 0`: command substitution would put a bare `$(` in the compose file, which compose interpolation treats as a variable reference and which then needs `$$` escaping. The pipeline form has NO `$` at all, so nothing to escape and nothing an operator can mis-copy. MEASURED that busybox `wc -l < file` prints an UNPADDED count in postgres:17-alpine (`0` / `1`, four fixture files), so `grep -qx 0` is an exact match, not a prefix match.

FAIL-CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION ON THE MISSING-SECRET PATH: if the secret is absent the `test -r` arm refuses first; even if that arm were removed, `wc -l < missing` fails and feeds `grep` empty input, which also fails. There is no input on which the guard exits 0 without having read a newline-free file.

LIVE MEASUREMENTS, scratch project `moe4b7yaml` under tmpdir, all resources removed (final residue containers 0 / volumes 0 / networks 0, scratch dir rm'd):
- `compose config` exit 0 — the block parses.
- NORMAL value: `up --detach --wait db` exit 0; guard `Exited`, db `Healthy`. The gate does not refuse everything.

DELIBERATE — a leading or embedded newline is mangled by the same command substitution only when trailing, but a value carrying one is an operator typo in every case observed, and admitting it would need the guard to distinguish positions it cannot safely print.
- UNSET and EMPTY: `up --detach db` exit 1, stderr byte-exact `secret "POSTGRES_PASSWORD" must declare either `file` or `environment`: invalid compose project`. THE SIBLING'S REFUSAL SURVIVES VERBATIM — adding the depended-on service did not change it, because compose refuses at project load, before any service is created.

implementationPlan.description:
PROVE IT AGAINST THE ACTUAL GENERATED SCAFFOLD, LIVE (DoD 1 and DoD 2).

ADAPT THE SIBLING'S PROBE; DO NOT WRITE A SECOND HARNESS. Its full source is in task-7693a195's comment-ed461460 (part 1) and comment-3a32dc34 (part 2): it materialises all generated files into a scratch project under `tmpdir()`, runs `docker compose up`, authenticates from the CONTAINER NETWORK ADDRESS with a wrong-password negative control, sweeps `docker inspect` and `compose config` for the planted value by count, and tears down with label-filtered zero-count assertions. Note its recorded correction: a loopback probe was INVALID because the wrong password also succeeded there; the container network address with the negative control is the valid form. Do not regress to loopback.

FOUR CLASSES, and each one is load-bearing:
(a) TRAILING NEWLINE — `docker compose up` now REFUSES at the guard, before the db initialises. Assert the guard's nonzero exit and that its message names POSTGRES_PASSWORD; assert the db container never reached a running state; assert no volume was created that would carry a half-initialised cluster.
(b) NORMAL random value — still authenticates. This is the positive control that stops (a) from being achieved by refusing everything.
(c) SPACE + `$` + TRAILING SPACE — still authenticates. Special characters are supported and must stay supported; only newlines are refused.
(d) WRONG PASSWORD — still refused by postgres with `password authentication failed` (exit 2), proving the auth probe can fail at all.

PIN A STABLE REFUSAL MARKER, ADDED 2026-09-10 (part 2 of the restore). Class (a)'s "nonzero exit and a message naming POSTGRES_PASSWORD" is WEAK ON ITS OWN: an unrelated guard failure — a missing or unreadable secret, a mount that did not appear, an image that cannot start — satisfies both while proving nothing about newlines. Emit a STABLE unsupported-newline marker from the guard and assert THAT, together with the guard stage, so the arm cannot be satisfied by a different failure. And assert the other direction separately: a missing or unreadable secret, or a guard that cannot start, must NOT authorise db startup either. Those are two distinct properties and a single "the guard failed" assertion covers neither.

AND THE UNSET/EMPTY ARM, which step 2 must not have weakened: `docker compose up --detach db` with unset AND with empty exits 1 with the sibling's exact stderr. Quote it verbatim.

NO VALUE-BEARING EVIDENCE MAY BE PERSISTED (the row says so, and epic rail 3). Compare counts and booleans, never values. Do not log the planted value, a prefix of it, a hash of it, or captured output that contains it. Do not commit a fixture carrying one.

TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH INCLUDING THE THROWING ONE (epic rail 4): `down --volumes --remove-orphans` exit 0, then label-filtered `docker ps --all --quiet`, `volume ls --quiet` and `network ls --quiet` all counting ZERO, then the scratch directory removed with its parent asserted to be `tmpdir()`. A probe that leaks a container makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

(a) TRAILING NEWLINE - `compose up --detach --wait db` exits nonzero at the guard. Guard logs carry POSTGRES_PASSWORD_NEWLINE_UNSUPPORTED, guard State.ExitCode != 0, database container State.Status == "created" with StartedAt still 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z.

(c) SPACE + `$` + TRAILING SPACE - identical, so special characters stay supported; only newlines are refused.
(d) WRONG PASSWORD - psql exit 2 with `password authentication failed`, run inside (b) and (c) so neither can be achieved by a probe that authenticates everything.

THE STABLE MARKER, and it is not decoration. I assert the marker AND the stage, so an unrelated guard failure cannot satisfy (a). The other direction is asserted SEPARATELY, as two more arms, because "the guard failed" covers neither:
